section_summary: The section begins with Ujigawa Electric Power Company financial statements and annexes concerning the property that secured its dollar bonds. Correspondence explains the wartime transfer of the company's assets and bond obligations, cancellation of the mortgages, and the selection of the Kisugawa power plant for reparations. Later letters concern American bondholders seeking information about claims, registration of their holdings, and possible recovery.

subfiles.title: Ujigawa Electric Power balance sheet, March 31, 1942
subfiles.about: Lists company assets, liabilities, reserves, and loss.
subfiles.summary: Balance sheet as of March 31, 1942, with total accounts of approximately ¥348.6 million.

subfiles.title: Ujigawa Electric Power profit and loss statement
subfiles.about: Reports operating income and expenses for October 1941 through March 1942.
subfiles.summary: Statement of profit and loss records electric supply operations, interest, asset valuation losses, retirement allowances, and a net loss.

subfiles.title: Comparative balance sheets of Kansai Electric Supply
subfiles.about: Compares assets and liabilities across successive semiannual accounting terms.
subfiles.summary: Multi-column statements track power plants, lines, investments, receivables, securities, deposits, and other accounts through wartime and postwar terms.

subfiles.title: Comparative profit and loss statements of Kansai Electric Supply
subfiles.about: Compares electric supply expenses and other financial results across semiannual terms.
subfiles.summary: Tables cover terms from 1942 into 1946, showing rising power purchase, distribution, personnel, tax, interest, and other expenses.

subfiles.title: Annex VII: Properties comprising the factory estate securing Ujigawa bonds
subfiles.about: Identifies properties formerly mortgaged to secure Ujigawa's first mortgage gold bonds.
subfiles.summary: The annex lists hydroelectric and steam plants, substations, switching stations, and other facilities owned by Japan Electric Generation and Transmission and Kansai Electric Supply. It records the cancellation date of the mortgages and notes that Kisugawa was selected for reparations.

subfiles.title: Annex VIII: Reparations selections of steam-electric power plants
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government, through Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Places selected steam-electric plants under Allied custody for possible removal as reparations.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum orders protection of equipment and records, preparation for shutdown, and arrangements to maintain power supply. The included list names Tsurumi, Kisugawa, and Azikawa plants.

subfiles.title: Annex IX cover
subfiles.about: Introduces the ensuing correspondence on Ujigawa bonds.
subfiles.summary: Annex divider.

subfiles.title: Industrial Bank of Japan letter on Ujigawa dollar bonds
subfiles.from: Takeo Kurusu, Industrial Bank of Japan
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Forwards wartime and postwar reports on Ujigawa bonds.
subfiles.summary: The bank sends two previously prepared Kansai Electric letters and offers further information.

subfiles.title: Kansai Electric letter forwarding bond report
subfiles.about: Requests delivery of a report to the National City Bank when communications reopen.
subfiles.summary: Kansai asks the trustee to convey its account of the dollar bonds.

subfiles.title: Kansai Electric report on Ujigawa first mortgage bonds
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Explains the wartime succession, bond payments, property transfers, government assumption, and mortgage cancellation.
subfiles.summary: Kansai describes its creation under the Electric Distribution Control Ordinance and its succession to Ujigawa's obligations. It explains wartime coupon payments into blocked accounts, the transfer of mortgaged property, the conversion of some bonds into domestic bonds, and Japanese government assumption of the remainder. It reports cancellation of the factory-estate mortgages in October 1943.

subfiles.title: Interest funds on Ujigawa dollar bonds
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Details interest funds due and deposited for 1942 and 1943 coupons.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates coupon funds, payments in Japan, and blocked account deposits.

subfiles.title: Kansai Electric forwarding letter on Kisugawa reparations
subfiles.about: Asks the trustee to forward notice of Kisugawa's reparations selection.
subfiles.summary: Kansai encloses its notice to the fiscal agent.

subfiles.title: Kansai Electric notice of Kisugawa reparations selection
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Advises that the formerly mortgaged Kisugawa plant was selected for reparations.
subfiles.summary: Kansai explains that Kisugawa was formerly part of the bond security but that government assumption of the bonds had annulled the mortgage before its reparations selection.

subfiles.title: Japan Electric notice of Kisugawa reparations selection
subfiles.from: Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Co.
subfiles.about: Reports the SCAP selection of Kisugawa and its former connection to Ujigawa bond security.
subfiles.summary: The plant owner says Kisugawa is on the reparations list and notes that cancellation of the mortgage ended its legal connection to the bonds.

subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum on steam-electric plant reparations
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; signed by John B. Cooley
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government, through Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Orders custody and preparation for possible removal of selected steam-electric plants.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the reparations directive and abbreviated plant list, including Kisugawa.

subfiles.title: State Department letter to National City Bank on Ujigawa bonds
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, Department of State
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese report and explains the government bond obligations and possible claims.
subfiles.summary: The Department says Japan assumed outstanding principal and interest, describes a moratorium on limitation periods, and notes that procedures for monetary-loss claims have not yet been established.

subfiles.title: Campbell inquiry about alien-property claim form
subfiles.about: Asks whether he must file Form APC-1C for his Japanese bond.
subfiles.summary: Campbell requests a claim form before the stated deadline.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Campbell
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains referral of Campbell's claim-form request and the Department's policy on foreign bonds.
subfiles.summary: State has asked the Office of Alien Property to send forms, will record Campbell's information, and points him toward the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: State Department referral of Campbell correspondence
subfiles.about: Refers Campbell's letters for action on claim forms.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the Office of Alien Property send Campbell the necessary forms.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Miyo Miyoshi
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains how her Tokyo Electric Light bond holding may be recorded and where she can seek claim information.
subfiles.summary: The Department offers to record the holding if Miyoshi establishes American citizenship, describes its policy on private and government bonds, and refers her to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Miyoshi follow-up requesting receipt
subfiles.about: Requests acknowledgment of her previously reported Tokyo Electric Light bond.
subfiles.summary: Miyoshi says she sent four copies of her holding information and asks for a receipt.

subfiles.title: Miyoshi report of Tokyo Electric Light bond
subfiles.about: Reports ownership of a $1,000 Tokyo Electric Light first mortgage bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the bond number, interest rate, maturity, and coupon dates.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Donald Grieve
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records Grieve's Tokyo Electric Light bond and explains possible bondholder and alien-property avenues.
subfiles.summary: The Department outlines its policy on foreign securities, describes the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and advises that holders may seek Office of Alien Property claim forms.

subfiles.title: Grieve report of Tokyo Electric Light bond
subfiles.about: Asks to be registered as owner of a $1,000 Tokyo Electric Light bond.
subfiles.summary: Grieve reports his bond and American citizenship.

subfiles.title: Watson inquiry about enemy-country bond claims
subfiles.about: Asks whether to file alien-property claims for Hungarian and German bonds.
subfiles.summary: Watson has already filed for Japanese bonds and seeks guidance before the deadline.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Watson
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Clarifies that its prior correspondence concerned policy rather than alien-property filing rules.
subfiles.summary: The only new development reported is transmission of a Japanese government bond report to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Emmy Lou Port, copy
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains policy on her Oriental Development bonds and asks for citizenship information.
subfiles.summary: The Department offers to record Port's holding, refers her to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and requests details of her American citizenship.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Emmy Lou Port, second copy
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department's response about Port's bonds and citizenship details.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the reply concerning bondholder representation and recording Port's holding.

subfiles.title: Port's Oriental Development bond claim inquiry
subfiles.about: Reports her guaranteed Oriental Development bond and asks for a claim form.
subfiles.summary: Port supplies the bond number and terms and requests filing instructions.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property referral of Port correspondence
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: Forwards Port's letter for direct State Department reply.
subfiles.summary: The office encloses Port's letter and its answer.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property reply to Port
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: Sends a claim form and explains filing periods and vested assets.
subfiles.summary: The office says it has vested property that may bear on the obligations, encloses Form APC-1C, and refers other matters to State.

subfiles.title: File note on Port's address
subfiles.about: Records an unsuccessful attempt to confirm Port's address.
subfiles.summary: Alien Property had only the recorded address and said its letter was not returned.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Port, corrected-address copy
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department's response concerning Port's Oriental Development bonds.
subfiles.summary: Another copy of the reply offers to record Port's holding and asks for citizenship particulars; the address bears handwritten corrections.

subfiles.title: Jacques Ruch residence statement
subfiles.about: States family residences relevant to Great Consolidated Electric Power bond holdings.
subfiles.summary: Ruch gives residence dates in France, Switzerland, and New York and mentions his family's U.S. ties.

subfiles.title: National City Bank letter to Jacques Ruch
subfiles.from: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Discusses custody and licensing information for Ruch's electric-power bonds.
subfiles.summary: The bank acknowledges the securities and cites a prior license; parts of the OCR are unclear.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to S. Albert Stern
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains the Department's position on Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department cannot give a definitive recovery answer, refers Stern to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and lists information holders may submit for its files.

subfiles.title: Stern inquiry about Imperial Japanese Government bonds
subfiles.about: Seeks information on recovering principal and interest on 1924 Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Stern asks how claims beyond alien-property assets might be handled.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Ralph Everett
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains policy and recordkeeping for Oriental Development bondholders.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes possible representation by the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and specifies bond and citizenship information it will record, while giving no definitive recovery forecast.

subfiles.title: Everett inquiry about Oriental Development debentures
subfiles.about: Asks about assets available for his guaranteed Oriental Development debentures.
subfiles.summary: Everett has filed alien-property claims but doubts vested assets will cover all claims.

subfiles.title: Paull inquiry about Ujigawa bonds
subfiles.about: Asks where to pursue a claim on two matured Ujigawa bonds.
subfiles.summary: The writer says the Office of Alien Property referred the matter to State and requests advice.

subfiles.title: National City Bank acknowledgment of Ujigawa report
subfiles.from: Stewart C. Pratt, National City Bank of New York
subfiles.to: Edward W. Doherty, Department of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Japanese report and requests notice of future claim procedures.
subfiles.summary: The bank notes the limitations moratorium and asks to be informed when monetary-loss claim procedures are established.
